data.narrative:
Sereact, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Ralf Gulde and Marc Tuscher, has raised $140M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, Exotec, and others) and one public comparable, reflecting the sector's mix of private and public participants.

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base of $140M and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x, implies a valuation of $266M. Peer-median methodology draws on three directly comparable Series B-stage robotics firms: Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, and Dexterity at $1.6B. The median of this peer set is $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B.

These methods produce a wide triangulated range: low of $226M, median of $1.0B, and high of $2.0B. The disparity between stage-progression ($266M) and peer-median ($1.8B) reflects the tension between conservative capital-deployed metrics and market comparables in a competitive frontier-tech sector. Key uncertainties center on peer selection appropriateness and whether Sereact's unit economics and go-to-market trajectory justify positioning at the peer median versus the lower bound of the range.
